Job Description
Sea, Air, and Land (SEAL) teams perform a range of duties in support of special operations missions and operate on, under, and from the sea, air,
and land, required skills include: combat diving, maritime operations, paradrop operations, air operations, land warfare, small unit tactics, and
close-quarters combat; conduct Special Operations Urban Combat (SOUC) and tactical mounted and dismounted operations; employ small arms,
Crew-Served Weapons (CSW), stand-off and indirect weapons, explosives, communications equipment; implement new technological
innovations into operations; perform tactical medicine, mission planning, intelligence-gathering; support joint and combined operations; operate
in Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Explosive (CBRNE) environments; and conduct counter-proliferation operations globally.

Special Warfare Operators (SO) perform maritime, land, and airborne special operations in urban, desert, jungle, arctic, undersea, and mountain environments; duties include: direct action, counterterrorism, special reconnaissance, foreign internal defense, counter insurgency, security force assistance, countering weapons of mass destruction, unconventional warfare, hostage rescue and recovery, and foreign humanitarian assistance. __________________________________________

Sea, Air, and Land (SEAL) teams perform a range of duties in support of special operations missions and operate on, under, and from the sea, air, and land, required skills include: combat diving, maritime operations, paradrop operations, air operations, land warfare, small unit tactics, and close-quarters combat; conduct Special Operations Urban Combat (SOUC) and tactical mounted and dismounted operations; employ small arms, Crew-Served Weapons (CSW), stand-off and indirect weapons, explosives, communications equipment; implement new technological innovations into operations; perform tactical medicine, mission planning, intelligence-gathering; support joint and combined operations; operate in Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Explosive (CBRNE) environments; and conduct counter-proliferation operations globally.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
